findings.title: should_block? writes to the DB and is called from a validator, so match_count is inflated
findings.body: `should_block?` increments `match_count`, sets `last_match_at` and saves the record, yet it is called from `EmailValidator#validate_each`. Validators should be side-effect free and may run many times per request. `UsersController#create` calls `user.valid?` and then `user.save`, which validates again, so one signup attempt bumps the counter twice (and any other `valid?` call adds more). The statistics are therefore wrong. Each validation also costs an extra SELECT, the uniqueness-validation query inside `record.save`, and an UPDATE. The stats update should happen once, at the point where the block is actually enforced, not inside validation.

findings.title: Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive, so blocking is trivially bypassed
findings.body: `BlockedEmail.where(email: email)` is an exact string match, and `User.new_from_params` stores the email as typed without downcasing. A blocked address such as `bad@spamclub.com` can be bypassed by signing up as `Bad@SpamClub.com`. Elsewhere in the codebase emails are normalised with `Email.downcase`. Both the stored blocked email and the lookup value should be normalised, for example downcased in `before_validation` and in `should_block?`.

findings.title: Non-atomic read-modify-write on match_count
findings.body: `record.match_count += 1; record.save` loads the value into Ruby, increments it and writes it back. Concurrent signup attempts with the same blocked email will lose increments. `increment_counter`, or an `update_all` with `match_count = match_count + 1`, would be atomic and skip the validation and uniqueness query on every hit.

findings.title: Invalid Ember dependent key 'rejectedEmails.@each'
findings.body: `@each` is only valid as `rejectedEmails.@each.someProp`, and the array-change key for a plain array is `rejectedEmails.[]`. With `'rejectedEmails.@each'` the `emailValidation` property may not recompute when `pushObject` adds a rejected email. In that case the UI would not flag the rejected address until `accountEmail` changes, which defeats the purpose of the feature.

findings.title: Mutable array declared on the controller prototype is shared
findings.body: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` in `.extend({...})` creates one array shared by every instance of the class, and it is never reset. Rejected emails therefore persist across any reuse of the controller, and a rejected address stays flagged even after the underlying issue (for example a blocklist change) is resolved. Initialise it per instance in `init`.

findings.title: Validator spec doesn't cover whitelist/blacklist paths or interaction with blocked check
findings.body: The domain whitelist and blacklist logic was moved out of `User` into `EmailValidator`, but the new spec only covers the blocked-email branch with a stubbed `BlockedEmail`. It does not test that whitelist or blacklist violations still add `not_allowed`, or that `should_block?` is skipped (so no stats update happens) when a domain error already exists. A regression in the moved code would go unnoticed.
